title: A Songbook for the Summer
premise: Vesper Sandoval, a single parent and owner of the failing Sandoval Books, dreads the annual Mariposa Creek family reunion where relatives measure worth in marriages and mortgages. Desperate for a shield, Vesper recruits Theo Marsh, the festival's visiting luthier and an old high school classmate, to pose as their date. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens through shared music, late-night inventory, and Vesper's daughter's quiet hope, until the fake relationship collapses under the weight of real feeling during the reunion's final toast. At the summer festival's closing concert, Vesper must finally speak the rehearsed sentence—asking for a real chance, out loud, in front of the whole town—and chooses love and visibility over the safe anonymity of a decade.
about_author: Elodie Vasquez is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent ten years recommending love stories before daring to write one. She now writes from a porch overlooking a lake, accompanied by an aging guitar and a stubborn cat named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper balances a failing bookshop, a skeptical eight-year-old daughter, and a mailbox full of reunion invitations, rehearsing a decade-old confession they've never dared speak. When Theo Marsh wanders into the shop seeking sheet music, an old spark flickers. Vesper impulsively proposes a fake date for the reunion. Emotional beat: longing disguised as practicality—the first crack in Vesper's armor of invisibility.

chapters.title: Plus-One, Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reunion's first day: Theo plays the role flawlessly, charming Vesper's disapproving aunts while Vesper performs a happiness that starts feeling less like acting. A shared dance to Theo's handcrafted guitar blurs every rule they set. Vesper's daughter bonds with Theo over songbooks, complicating everything. Emotional beat: the dangerous warmth of being seen—and the terror that the arrangement is becoming real.

chapters.title: What the Toast Exposed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the reunion's climactic dinner, a relative's toast mocks Vesper's 'settled' life, and Theo—defending them too fiercely—accidentally reveals genuine feelings in front of everyone. Vesper, humiliated and cornered, ends the arrangement publicly and flees. Theo, packing to leave after the festival, realizes the fake contract was his own denial. Emotional beat: the collapse—duty to pride versus love, with the festival's end looming as a deadline.

chapters.title: The Last Set
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On the festival's closing night, Theo's truck is packed and the stage lights are on. Vesper's daughter stages a small intervention, and Vesper walks into the crowd during Theo's final song and finally speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud—asking to be loved, visibly, on purpose. Theo steps offstage into the applause. Epilogue hint: the bookshop's window now reads 'Two Copies of Everything.' Emotional beat: belonging claimed, identity chosen, love outrunning duty.
